findings.title: enableSqlExpressions has dead/confusing logic that always returns false
findings.body:
The newly added `enableSqlExpressions` function reads:

```go
func enableSqlExpressions(h *ExpressionQueryReader) bool {
    enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)
    if enabled {
        return false
    }
    return false
}
```

The function unconditionally returns `false` regardless of the feature flag's state. The `enabled` variable and the `if enabled { return false }` branch are dead code (both branches return `false`). This is confusing because:
1. The function name suggests it checks whether SQL expressions should be enabled.
2. A future maintainer is likely to interpret this as buggy logic and "fix" it (e.g. by returning `enabled` or `!enabled`), which could accidentally re-enable the vulnerable code path.
3. The `featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions` check is functionally meaningless.

For a security hardening PR, the intent should be expressed unambiguously. Either simplify to `return false` with a comment referencing CVE-2024-9264, or rename and invert the logic so the dead branches are removed.

findings.title: Misleading error message for a security-driven disablement
findings.body: When SQL expressions are rejected the user-visible error is `sqlExpressions is not implemented`. The feature is not merely unimplemented; it has been intentionally disabled to mitigate CVE-2024-9264 (RCE/LFI). A user reading the error or a downstream log/alert may conclude the feature was forgotten rather than turned off for security reasons. The message should clearly state that the feature is disabled (e.g. reference the CVE / security release) so that operators and users understand why a previously working dashboard now errors.

findings.title: No tests added for the SQL-expression disablement
findings.body: The PR introduces a new code path (`enableSqlExpressions` gating `QueryTypeSQL` in `ReadQuery`) but adds no tests. For a security fix landing in the primary repo this is a significant gap: there is nothing in the test suite that asserts a SQL expression query is rejected, and nothing that documents the expected behaviour for downstream users / release notes readers. At minimum a test exercising `ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery` with `QueryTypeSQL` and asserting the new error should be added; ideally also a test covering `UnmarshalSQLCommand`/`NewSQLCommand` to confirm the in-memory DB stub returns the expected errors.

findings.title: TablesList logs a misleading "error serializing sql" for the stubbed DB
findings.body: `TablesList` calls `duckDB.RunCommands(...)` and, on error, logs `"error serializing sql"` and returns `fmt.Errorf("error serializing sql: %s", err.Error())`. With the new `DB` stub this branch is hit on every invocation because `RunCommands` always returns `errors.New("not implemented")`. The log/return message implies a SQL serialization issue occurred, which is misleading: nothing was actually serialized or attempted against DuckDB. The wording should reflect that the SQL expression backend is disabled (or simply that the operation is not implemented).

findings.title: UnmarshalSQLCommand bypass path may not be covered by the ReadQuery gate
findings.body: `UnmarshalSQLCommand` is still present in `pkg/expr/sql_command.go` and still constructs a `SQLCommand` via `NewSQLCommand`. The security gate added in this PR only lives inside `ReadQuery` (the `ExpressionQueryReader` path). If `UnmarshalSQLCommand` is reachable from any other request handling code (legacy path, direct test usage, future callers), the gate in `ReadQuery` will not protect that path. It happens to be safe today only because `NewSQLCommand` -> `sql.TablesList` -> `RunCommands` returns the "not implemented" stub error, which is a fragile defense-in-depth arrangement. The PR should either verify that `UnmarshalSQLCommand` is dead code and remove it, or add the same disablement check inside it explicitly.
